The fulfilment of mandatory requirements by farmers and their validations is an essential condition to qualify as beneficiary and receive the benefits under the scheme. The States/UTs are mandated to enroll the beneficiaries and validate and verify their data. Funds are released on the basis of beneficiaries identified and verified by the States/UTs. A robust grievance redressal mechanism has been established under the PM-KISAN Scheme to address the grievances of farmers. Farmers may register their grievances through the PM-KISAN portal, where they are promptly examined and resolved by the concerned officers of the respective State/UT Governments. In addition, farmers may also lodge their grievances through the CPGRAMS portal, and such grievances are addressed and resolved in a timely manner. Since inception of the Scheme, 6,151 grievances have been received on PM-KISAM portal in Saran district all of which have been resolved, and in Siwan District, 2,751 grievances have been received on PM-KISAM portal out of which 2,749 have been resolved.
In order to ensure that no eligible farmer is left out, the Government of India undertakes saturation drives in coordination with the States/UTs, including Bihar. A major nationwide saturation drive was undertaken from 15th November 2023 under the Viksit Bharat Sankalp Yatra (VBSY), during which, more than 1 Cr. farmers were included under PM-KISAN, including 3,44,180 in Bihar. Further, under the Government’s 100 days initiative in 2024, over 25 lakh eligible farmers were added under the PM-KISAN scheme including 25,099 in Bihar. A special drive was also conducted in September 2024 to clear the pending self-registration cases, which resulted in the addition of over 30 lakh new farmers, including 33,614 in Bihar. A nationwide saturation drive has also been undertaken from 1st June, 2026 under PM-KISAN alongwith the “Khet Bachao Abhiyaan” to expand the coverage of eligible farmers under the scheme which resulted in the addition of about 17 lakh new farmers, including 58,556 in Bihar. In addition, States/UTs, including Bihar, also undertake saturation drives from time to time to identify and facilitate the enrolment of eligible farmers completing all mandatory conditions under the Scheme.

articles.full_content:
The total number of applications received, and participants enrolled under Phase I of the National Artificial Intelligence (AI) Skilling Initiative as on date is 60,253.
The total number of participants who have completed 2 Modules of Phase I of the programme are 4620 and those who have completed all 4 Modules of Phase I of the programme are 552.
Phase I of the programme comprises four modules with a total duration of 33 hours, delivered through two learning platforms. The details of the Modules of Phase I are as under: -
• Module 1: AI Essentials – gain practical skills to boost daily productivity, synthesize data, and create content.
• Module 2: Prompting Essentials – framework to write professional prompts.
• Module 3: Introduction to Generative AI – grasp Large Language Model (LLM) fundamentals and responsible AI guidelines.
• Module 4: Generative AI Leader – master workflow automation and strategic Gen AI organisational transformation.
The details of Phase II, including the curriculum, modules and course duration, are under finalisation.
The curriculum has been jointly designed and developed by the IICT and private sector partners to impart foundational and practical AI skills. The advanced skilling component is conducted by IICT for joint certification.
The Government’s role has been to provide strategic direction and facilitating the implementation of the programme through IICT with the objective of enhancing AI literacy and equipping students with industry-relevant digital skills.
The information was provided by the Minister of State for Information and Broadcasting and Parliamentary Affairs, Dr. L. Murugan, in a written reply to a Question asked by Adv Gowaal Kagada Padavi in Lok Sabha today.

Government Promotes Sustainable Growth of Data Centres through Energy-Efficient and Clean Energy Measures
articles.full_content:
In line with Hon’ble Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi's vision, the Government is democratising the development and usage of technology.
Data centres are an important & integral component of the overall Digital India Infrastructure ecosystem. The Data Centre industry in India has been growing at a steady pace. The rapid growth of AI and high-performance computing is driving increasing demand for data centre capacity in the country.
Data centres are located across the country majorly in areas such as Mumbai, Navi Mumbai, Chennai, Hyderabad, Bengaluru, Delhi NCR and Jamnagar. The installed capacity has grown from 375 MW in 2020 to current capacity of about 1575 MW.
The Data Centre industry is now further expanding in States like Andhra Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh & West Bengal which are coming up as new investment destinations.
The current data centres capacity across the country is less than 1% of the current installed power capacity. As per Central Electricity Authority (CEA), Ministry of Power (MoP), the power demand of data centres is estimated to be about 17 GW up to 2031-32.
Energy Efficiency & Water Conservation
• The Government of India is promoting renewable energy through measures such as Green Energy Open Access Rules, Green Energy Corridor Scheme, Green Term Ahead Market (GTAM), National Green Hydrogen Mission, National Programme on High Efficiency Solar PV Modules, Offshore Wind VGF Scheme and Solar Park Scheme.
• Sustainable Harnessing and Advancement of Nuclear Energy for Transforming India (SHANTI) Act, has been enacted to strengthen reliable clean power for emerging sectors such as AI and data centres, including future deployment of Small Modular and Micro Nuclear Reactors.
• Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS), through technical committee LITD 31 (Cloud Computing, IT & Data Centres), has published a series of Indian Standards on Power Usage Effectiveness, Carbon Usage Effectiveness (CUE), Cooling Efficiency Ratio (CER), Water Usage Effectiveness (WUE) related to data centres.
• The Bureau of Energy Efficiency (BEE) has notified Energy Conservation Building Code (ECBC 2017) and Energy Conservation & Sustainable Building Code (ECSBC 2024) prescribing energy efficiency and water conservation norms for buildings, including provisions relevant to data centres.
• The water requirement of data centres depends on the type of cooling technologies deployed. Regulation and control of groundwater extraction, including for industrial purposes, is governed by the guidelines issued by the Ministry of Jal Shakti. With the advancement of AI infrastructure, data centre cooling systems are also adopting advanced technologies such as direct-to-chip liquid cooling, adiabatic cooling, immersion cooling and closed-loop liquid cooling systems.

Under the Government of India’s Skill India Mission (SIM) , the Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship (MSDE) delivers skill, re-skill and up-skill training through an extensive network of skill development centres under various schemes, viz. Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Vikas Yojana (PMKVY), Jan Shikshan Sansthan (JSS), National Apprenticeship Promotion Scheme (NAPS) and Craftsman Training Scheme (CTS) through Industrial Training Institutes (ITIs), to all the sections of the society across the country including the state of Kerala. The SIM aims at enabling youth of India to get future ready and equipped with industry relevant skills. Some of the key schemes under SIM are:
Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Vikas Yojana (PMKVY): The PMKVY Scheme is for imparting skill development training through Short-Term Training (STT) and up-skilling and re-skilling through Recognition of Prior Learning (RPL) to youth across the country including the state of Kerala.
Jan Shikshan Sansthan (JSS) Scheme : The scheme aims to impart vocational skills to the non-literates, neo-literates and the persons having a rudimentary level of education and school dropouts up to 12th standard in the age group of 15-45 years, with due age relaxation in case of “Divyangjan” and other deserving cases. Priority is given to Women, SC, ST, OBC and Minorities in the rural areas and urban low-income areas.
National Apprenticeship Promotion Scheme (NAPS): This Scheme is for promoting apprenticeship training and increasing the engagement of apprentices by providing financial support for payment of stipend to apprentices. Training consists of Basic Training and On-the- Job Training / Practical Training at the workplace in the industry.
Craftsmen Training Scheme (CTS): This scheme is for providing long-term training through Industrial Training Institutes (ITIs) across the country. The ITIs offer a range of vocational/skill training courses covering many economic sectors with the objective to provide a skilled workforce to the industry as well as self-employment of youth.

A key focus of the scheme is skilling in new-age and future-oriented technologies. Under PMKVY 4.0, over 600 courses have been introduced in areas such as Artificial Intelligence (AI), Drone Technology, 5G, Solar Energy, Additive Manufacturing (3D Printing), Semiconductors, and the Internet of Things (IoT). As on 30 June 2026, more than 5.44 lakh candidates have been trained in these sectors. PMKVY 4.0 aims to equip candidates with industry-relevant skills and enable them to pursue diverse career pathways through skill courses embedded with On-the-Job Training (OJT) for practical workplace exposure.
PMKVY 4.0 is a demand driven scheme, wherein training targets are approved based on the proposals submitted by the Project Implement Agencies, after taking the skill gap into account. Under PMKVY4.0, as on 30.06.2026, ₹ 414.86 Crore have been utilized for training under future/new edge job roles including drone technology, artificial intelligence and green energy maintenance. To promote new age courses, the prevalent highest training cost as per Common Norms of ₹49 per hour is provided to training providers to ensure access to suitable training infrastructure, tools, equipment, and qualified trainers required for implementing the advanced job roles.

Integration of Artificial Intelligence Into The Skill Development Ecosystem
articles.full_content:
The Government has systematically integrated Artificial Intelligence (AI) into the national skilling ecosystem through the following measures:
Skill India Digital Hub (SIDH)
Skill India Digital Hub (SIDH) has been launched as a unified Digital Public Infrastructure (DPI) and serves as the core platform for technology-driven skilling. Under SIDH, the Ministry launched the Skilling for AI Readiness (SOAR) programme on 22.07.2025 to promote AI literacy and prepare learners for an AI-enabled future. The programme initially comprised four fully online, self-paced, NSQF-aligned and credit-linked foundational learner courses – AI to be Aware, AI to Acquire, AI to Aspire, and AI for Educators. The programme was subsequently expanded to include 50 AI and AI application-oriented qualifications covering AI for jobs, workplace productivity, sector-specific applications, inclusivity, and contextualised AI applications for the unorganised sector. As on 06.08.2026, a total of 5,17,477 learners have enrolled and 1,00,664 learners have been certified under the SOAR courses available on SIDH.
Under Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Vikas Yojana (PMKVY) 4.0, emphasis has been placed on industry-aligned and future-ready skills, including Artificial Intelligence (AI), Machine Learning, Data Science, Internet of Things (IoT), Cyber Security, Cloud Computing, Semiconductors, Drones, Electric Vehicles (EVs), Green Hydrogen, Robotics, AR/VR and 5G Technologies. The scheme framework incorporates demand-driven skilling, enhanced industry participation, mandatory On-the-Job Training (OJT) in applicable job roles, promotion of apprenticeship opportunities, and strengthened digital monitoring mechanisms through the Skill India ecosystem. articles.full_content:
'Bharat GI' Banner Launched: Ministry of MSME and DPIIT to Bring Regional GI Products to ONDC and GeM
In a significant step towards unlocking the economic potential of India's rich heritage of Geographical Indication (GI) products, the Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises and the Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT), Ministry of Commerce and Industry, signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) on 05 th August,2026 at Vanijya Bhawan, New Delhi. The MoU was signed by Md. Salik Parwaiz, Director, Ministry of MSME and Shri Karan Thapar, Director, IPR Division, DPIIT, in the presence of senior officials of both organisations.
DPIIT is the nodal department for the registration and legal protection of Geographical Indications in India under the Geographical Indications of Goods (Registration and Protection) Act, 1999, while Ministry of MSME is the nodal ministry for steering the growth, financial health and overall development of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises, traditional industries and artisans across the country. Both sides recognise that while the legal registration of GIs protects regional identity, maximising their economic value requires a coordinated effort to transition these products from localised crafts into scalable, commercially viable and export-ready enterprises. The MoU accordingly establishes a collaborative framework to accelerate the commercialisation, quality standardisation and market penetration of Indian GI products, thereby enhancing the livelihoods of indigenous artisans, weavers and producers, while also strengthening the One District One Product (ODOP) ecosystem in the country.
As joint initiatives, both organisations will work towards integrating ODOP in their programme design and interventions, collaboratively facilitate the onboarding of GI collectives and authorised users onto the Open Network for Digital Commerce (ONDC) and the Government e-Marketplace (GeM) under a dedicated “Bharat GI” banner, and co-sponsor dedicated GI Pavilions at national and international trade expos, buyer-seller meets and exhibitions for domestic and global marketing of GI products.
The MoU represents a significant step towards aligning the Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade’s (DPIIT) mandate for intellectual property protection with the Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises’ (MSME) mandate for enterprise development. The collaboration is expected to strengthen India’s Geographical Indications (GI) ecosystem by facilitating capacity building, digital enablement and enhanced market access for artisans, weavers and producer collectives. It will further support the integration of GI products with premium domestic and international markets, contributing to the vision of Aatmanirbhar Bharat and Vocal for Local .

articles.full_content:
The Government has undertaken several initiatives to promote textile recycling, adoption of recycling technologies and the transition towards a circular economy in the textile sector:
i) In the Union Budget 2026–27, the Hon'ble Finance Minister announced the ‘Tex-Eco Initiative’ to promote a globally competitive and sustainable textiles and apparel sector. The initiative aims to support innovative technologies for the circular economy, including textile waste management, recycling and value addition, development of recycled fibres, new materials, sustainable packaging and other high-value products from discarded textiles, in collaboration with research institutions, Textile Research Associations, Centres of Excellence, industry, start-ups and other stakeholders.
ii) The Ministry of Textiles has undertaken a study titled “Mapping of Textile Waste Value Chain in India”. The report estimates the generation of textile waste from pre-consumer sources such as manufacturing waste as well as post-consumer waste.
iii) The Government has also constituted an Environment, Social and Governance (ESG) Task Force to deliberate on sustainable production, certification and exports, besides facilitating industry-centric programmes such as Circular Samvaad and the Cluster Exchange Mechanism.
iv) The Government is also promoting textile recycling and sustainable manufacturing through policy support, research, innovation and capacity-building initiatives, including:
• The UNIDO-Global Environment Facility (GEF) project on eliminating hazardous chemicals from the textile fashion supply chain;
• The UNEP supported In-Tex India Project for Accelerating the Transition of the Indian Textile Sector towards Circularity using Life Cycle Assessment (LCA) and Product Environmental Footprint (PEF);
• Support for environmentally sustainable research and development under the National Technical Textiles Mission (NTTM);
• Development of a sustainability framework for PM MITRA Parks; and
• Promotion of upcycled products in Government procurement through an MoU among the Textiles Committee, Standing Conference of Public Enterprises (SCOPE) and Government e-Marketplace (GeM).
These initiatives are sector-wide and are intended to facilitate technology adoption, research, innovation, sustainable manufacturing and circular economy practices across the textile value chain.
This information was provided by THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR TEXTILES SHRI PABITRA MARGHERITA in a written reply to a question in Lok Sabha today.

Climate Correction is the Need of the Hour”: Prof. Chetan Singh Solanki Calls for Responsible Consumption and Climate Action at CURAJ
articles.full_content:
“Climate correction is the right action at the moment.” With this powerful message, Prof. Chetan Singh Solanki, former Professor at IIT Bombay and popularly known as the “Solar Man of India,” called upon students and the academic community to adopt responsible consumption practices and take meaningful action to address climate change.
The School of Earth Sciences, Central University of Rajasthan (CURAJ), hosted an inspiring and thought-provoking session with Prof. Solanki, who has been undertaking the Climate Satyagraha Yatra since 2020, with the larger objective of creating awareness and inspiring collective action for a sustainable future.
Vice-Chancellor Prof. Anand Bhalerao emphasised that addressing environmental challenges requires not only technological solutions but also responsible individual behaviour and collective commitment towards sustainable living. He appreciated the initiative of the School of Earth Sciences in bringing important conversations on climate change and sustainability to the university community.
During his address, Prof. Solanki spoke extensively about the concept of “Happy Living” and urged students to rethink their relationship with consumption. He observed that while technology, software and automated systems are rapidly expanding into every sphere of life, the quality of air, water and soil is simultaneously deteriorating.
Drawing attention to the growing population, declining soil fertility and shrinking land under cultivation, he cautioned that the present pace of consumption could pose serious challenges to the availability of food and natural resources for future generations.
Describing the Earth as having a “fever”, Prof. Solanki said that the rising global temperature and climate change are already visible through increasing floods, extreme weather events and changing and erratic rainfall patterns. He stressed that climate change is no longer a distant threat but a reality that demands immediate corrective action.
Prof. Solanki encouraged students to make small but meaningful changes in their everyday consumption habits. Giving an example, he explained that not purchasing new clothes for one year can help save approximately 20,000 litres of water, 52.5 kg of carbon dioxide emissions and 3.75 kg of chemicals, thereby demonstrating how individual choices can contribute to environmental conservation.
As the founder of the Finite Earth Movement, Prof. Solanki motivated students to take a pledge to “consume within the limits” and become responsible participants in the movement for climate correction. He emphasised that sustainable living is not about compromising happiness, but about redefining happiness through responsible choices and mindful consumption.
Prof. Solanki is currently leading the 100-day Bharat Climate Satyagraha Yatra from May 13 to August 20, 2026, travelling across India’s quadrilateral and covering 51 cities to mobilise citizens, particularly young people, towards meaningful climate action.

Physical Challans Dispensed with for Voluntary Duty Payments from 1 August 2026 DGFT–ICEGATE API Integration Enables Direct Access to Authenticated Customs Duty Payment Records
In a significant Ease of Doing Business measure for exporters, the Directorate General of Foreign Trade (DGFT) has removed the requirement of submitting physical duty payment challans while applying for Export Obligation Discharge Certificates (EODC) under the Advance Authorisation (AA) and Export Promotion Capital Goods (EPCG) Schemes. Licence-wise voluntary duty payment data received from Customs/ICEGATE has been integrated with DGFT’s online systems, enabling authenticated verification of such payments directly against the concerned authorisation.
For voluntary duty payments made on or after 1 August 2026, exporters will no longer be required to submit physical challans along with their applications for closure of authorisations. Authenticated payment details will be made available to exporters on the DGFT Customer Portal, enabling them to verify that the payment has been correctly mapped to the concerned authorisation before filing the application.
The same authenticated payment record will be available to the Regional Authorities on the DGFT Back Office, eliminating the need for manual verification of payment particulars. This is expected to facilitate faster processing, reduce avoidable correspondence and bring greater consistency in decision-making across DGFT Regional Authorities.
The digital facility has been implemented through an API-based data exchange between DGFT and ICEGATE, under which duty payment particulars are transmitted electronically from Customs systems to DGFT’s EODC processing workflow. The replacement of manual submission and verification with authenticated digital records is expected to shorten processing timelines, improve data accuracy, minimise human intervention and enhance transparency in the closure process.
The measure is also expected to reduce transaction costs and compliance burden for exporters by reducing documentation, follow-up and physical interface, particularly benefiting MSME exporters handling closure formalities in-house. Trade Notice No. 15/2026-27 dated 5 August 2026 has been issued by DGFT for information of exporters and other stakeholders.
The initiative is part of the Government’s broader digital transformation agenda for trade facilitation, aimed at creating a more efficient, predictable and trust-based regulatory environment. By strengthening integration between trade-related digital systems and reducing reliance on physical documentation, the measure reinforces the vision of “Minimum Government, Maximum Governance” and enables exporters to focus on trade and growth.

articles.full_content:
From January 2025, survey design has been strengthened to provide monthly estimates at the all-India level and quarterly estimates for both rural and urban areas, in addition to annual estimates
The Employment-Unemployment Surveys (EUS) previously conducted by the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI) were the principal source of labour market statistics in the country till 2011-12. In view of the growing need for more frequent and timely labour market indicators, and based on the recommendations of the National Statistical Commission (NSC), MoSPI introduced the Periodic Labour Force Survey (PLFS) in 2017 after due deliberations by expert committees constituted for developing the survey methodology and sample design.
PLFS introduced methodological improvements over the earlier EUS, including a rotational panel sampling design for urban areas, Computer-Assisted Personal Interviewing (CAPI) with in-built validation checks, collection of information on hours worked, and changes in the sampling design and schedule of enquiry to generate periodic labour force estimates. Further, from January 2025, the survey design has been strengthened to provide monthly estimates at the all-India level and quarterly estimates for both rural and urban areas, in addition to annual estimates.
The concepts and definitions relating to employment, unemployment and labour force participation adopted in PLFS continue to remain consistent with those followed in the earlier EUS and are based on the recommendations of the Committee of Experts on Unemployment Estimates (Dantwala Committee) as well as the relevant international standards adopted by the International Conference of Labour Statisticians (ICLS). Accordingly, the PLFS continues to support analysis of long-term labour market trends.
Further, while disseminating the PLFS results through the Annual Reports, Quarterly Bulletins and Monthly Bulletins, MoSPI has advised users to exercise appropriate caution while making direct comparisons between PLFS and the earlier EUS estimates, as differences in survey design and methodology may influence the estimates.
MoSPI continuously engages with economists, researchers, subject-matter experts and other stakeholders, and the feedback received is considered while improving survey methodology, sampling design, questionnaire design, data collection and dissemination practices to enhance the quality, reliability and relevance of labour market statistics.
This information was given by the Minister of State (Independent Charge) of the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation, Minister of State (Independent Charge) of the Ministry of Planning and Minister of State in the Ministry of Culture Rao Inderjit Singh in the Rajya Sabha today.

articles.title: AVERAGE GROUNDWATER CONSUMPTION AND ITS QUALITY IN THE COUNTRY
articles.full_content:
The Central Ground Water Board (CGWB), jointly with the concerned State Governments/UT Administrations, assesses the Dynamic Ground Water Resources of the country. The assessment estimates total Annual Ground Water Recharge, Annual Extractable Ground Water Resource and Annual Ground Water Extraction for irrigation, domestic and industrial uses. As per Dynamic Ground Water Resources Assessment, 2025, total Annual Ground Water Recharge of the country has been assessed as 449 Billion Cubic Metres (BCM), Annual Extractable Ground Water Resource as 408 BCM and Annual Ground Water Extraction for all uses (representing groundwater consumption) as 247 BCM. Of total Annual Ground Water Extraction, 215 BCM (87%) is used for irrigation, 28 BCM (11%) for domestic purposes, including drinking water, and 4 BCM (2%) for industrial purposes.
The Dynamic Ground Water Resources Assessment does not assess groundwater consumption on a per-capita basis. However, it assesses the Stage of Ground Water Extraction, which is the ratio of Annual Ground Water Extraction to Annual Extractable Ground Water Resource. As per the Assessment, the Stage of Ground Water Extraction for the country is 60.63 per cent. The Stage of Ground Water Extraction is higher than the national average in 9 States/UTs viz Punjab, Rajasthan, Haryana, Delhi, Puducherry, Tamil Nadu, Uttar Pradesh, Chandigarh and Karnataka. Based on district-wise aggregation of the assessment results, 281 districts have a Stage of Ground Water Extraction higher than the national average. The State/UT-wise and district wise details are available at the following link: https://cgwb.gov.in/PQ/Stage_of_Groundwater_Extraction_more_than-Annexure.pdf
As per the Assessment of Water Resources of India, 2024 carried out by the Central Water Commission (CWC), the estimated average annual per capita water availability for the year 2021 was 1,573.19 cubic metres.
The Central Ground Water Board (CGWB) generates groundwater quality data through its groundwater quality monitoring programme and various scientific studies in accordance with the approved Standard Operating Procedure (SoP), which provides for more frequent and denser sampling, particularly in vulnerable areas. Groundwater quality varies spatially and temporally depending upon local hydrogeological and other conditions. As per the Annual Ground Water Quality Report, 2025, groundwater in the country is generally potable and nearly 99 per cent of the monitoring stations have groundwater quality suitable for irrigation use. Since the occurrence and spatial distribution of individual contaminants vary considerably, CGWB does not classify or rank States or districts in terms of the poorest groundwater quality. Parameter-wise groundwater quality data for the country, including the State of Bihar, are available in the Annual Ground Water Quality Report, 2025, which can be accessed at the following link: https://cgwb.gov.in/cgwbpnm/public/uploads/documents/1762854375262680475file

articles.title: Redesigning of PMKVY Courses
articles.full_content:
Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship (MSDE) has been implementing its flagship scheme Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Vikas Yojana (PMKVY), since 2015, for imparting skill development training through Short-Term Training (STT) and up-skilling and re-skilling through Recognition of Prior Learning (RPL), to all sections of the society. Under PMKVY 4.0 which is under implementation since FY 2022-23, the focus is on imparting training in emerging and new-age courses such as Artificial Intelligence, semiconductors, electronics, green energy, electric vehicles, drones, cybersecurity, robotics, etc., as per the industry requirement. To meet emerging technology demands, 600+ new-age and futuristic courses have been introduced. As on 30.06.2026, around 5.44 lakh candidates have been trained in new-age and futuristic job roles under PMKVY 4.0 across the country.
Under PMKVY scheme, placements were tracked in the Short-Term Training (STT) component in the first three versions of the Scheme - PMKVY 1.0, PMKVY 2.0 and PMKVY 3.0, implemented from FY 2015-16 to FY 2021-22. In these versions of PMKVY, out of 56.89 lakh candidates that have been certified in STT, 24.37 lakh candidates were reported placed which makes the overall placement rate at 42.8%. Under PMKVY 4.0 which is under implementation since FY 2022-23, the focus is to empower trained candidates to choose their varied career path and they are suitably oriented for the same through On-Job Training (OJT) embedded industry relevant skill courses.
PMKVY was evaluated by NITI Aayog in October 2020 across several states. As per the study, about 94% of the employers surveyed reported they would hire more candidates trained under PMKVY. Further, 52% of the candidates who were placed in full time/part-time employment and oriented under the RPL component received higher salary or felt that they will get higher salary compared to their un-certified peers. Also, a third-party impact evaluation of PMKVY 2.0 (2016-20) was also conducted by the Indian Institute of Public Administration (IIPA). As per the evaluation, about 70.5% surveyed candidates received placement in their desired skill sector.
Further, a third-party evaluation of PMKVY 4.0 conducted by the Arun Jaitley National Institute of Financial Management (AJNIFM) in 2025 observed that PMKVY training has led to a measurable improvement in employment outcomes for Short-Term Training (STT) candidates, with the combined share of employed and self-employed respondents increasing from 26.6% prior to training to 45.4% post-training, reflecting a significant rise of 18.8 % points. Moreover, 41.4% of STT candidates and 48.9% of RPL candidates reported an increase in income following PMKVY training and certification.

articles.title: AI-Based Training and Skill Development Initiatives
articles.full_content:
Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship (MSDE), through National Council for Vocational Education and Training (NCVET), Directorate General of Training (DGT) and under PMKVY 4.0, has initiated multiple programmes for Artificial Intelligence (AI)-based training and skilling across sectors:
1. Under the NCVET-regulated ecosystem, 116 NSQF-aligned and NSQC-approved Qualifications, National Occupational Standards (NOSs) and Micro-Credentials relating to Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning are presently in place, covering domains such as Generative AI, Agentic AI, Large Language Models (LLMs), Prompt Engineering, Machine Learning, Deep Learning, Natural Language Processing, Computer Vision, Robotics and Automation, AI Security, AI Ethics, AI Governance, and sector-specific AI applications.
2. Under the Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Vikas Yojana (PMKVY) 4.0, training is imparted in AI and AI-enabled job roles across sectors such as IT-ITES, Telecom and Life Sciences, with job roles developed in consultation with industry and Sector Skill Councils. As of 30.06.2026 under PMKVY 4.0, 53,449 candidates been trained/oriented and 25,466 candidates certified in AI related job roles.
3. The Directorate General of Training (DGT) has introduced AI into vocational training through the Artificial Intelligence Programming Assistant (1-year) course, a 240-hour Generative AI course, and a 7.5-hour AI micro-credential for trainees in Industrial Training Institutes (ITIs). The compulsory Employability Skills curriculum has also been revised to include modules on AI and Green Skills. MoSPI signs two MoUs with IDEAS, ISI Kolkata for undertaking Research Studies
articles.full_content:
Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI) signed two Memoranda of Understanding (MoUs) with Institute of Data Engineering, Analytics and Science Foundation (IDEAS), Indian Statistical Institute (ISI), Kolkata for undertaking Research Studies.
Shri Agnimitra Biswas, Chief Executive Officer, IDEAS and Shri Prasoon Verma, Director, Training Unit, Capacity Development Division, MoSPI signed the MoUs. The signing ceremony was graced by the presence of Shri P. R. Meshram, Director General (Data Governance), MoSPI and Shri R. Rajesh, Additional Director General, Capacity Development Division, MoSPI.
This collaborative initiative is an innovative, knowledge sharing platform between MoSPI and IDEAS, wherein MoSPI will provide financial assistance & data support and IDEAS will develop a desktop-based software tool to do GDP Nowcasting and a harmonised indicator framework linking administrative data on government health, nutrition and well-being schemes with household-level NSS data.
This collaboration aims to deep dive into the various statistics released by MoSPI and provide harmonisation with other data sources, emphasising the data-driven decision-making initiative by the Government of India for Viksit Bharat @ 2047.
